Political analysts note that the proposal could face significant hurdles, as dismantling a federal agency typically requires congressional approval and may involve complex legislative processes. Lawmakers from both parties have expressed varying degrees of support and opposition, emphasizing concerns about potential disruptions to services and the precedent such an action would set. The president’s remarks have sparked debate over the balance between governmental reform and the continuity of public functions, with the issue expected to be a focal point in upcoming legislative discussions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: NAZA documentary wins Special Jury Prize at Venice Film Festival
content:
The documentary *NAZA*, which examines the conflict in Gaza and alleges acts of genocide by Israel, was awarded the Special Jury Prize at the 81st Venice International Film Festival. The ceremony, held in early September, recognized the film among a slate of international entries for its investigative approach and cinematic execution.

The award, presented by the festival’s jury chaired by acclaimed director Luca Guadagnino, highlights the growing attention to Middle‑East reportage in global cinema. *NAZA*’s director, Yossi Koren, accepted the prize on behalf of the production team, noting the film’s aim to document civilian experiences during the recent hostilities. Organizers indicated that the Special Jury Prize is intended to honor works that combine artistic merit with pressing social relevance, positioning *NAZA* alongside other critically acclaimed documentaries featured at the festival.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israel bombs southern Lebanon as US‑mediated talks postponed
content:
Washington‑mediated negotiations between Israel and Lebanon have been delayed, with officials confirming that the next round of talks scheduled for this week will not take place as planned. The United States, which has been facilitating the dialogue since the initial contact in early 2024, cited logistical challenges and the need for additional preparation time as the primary reasons for the postponement. Both Israeli and Lebanese delegations were informed of the change through diplomatic channels, and a new date for the session is expected to be proposed within the coming days.

The talks, aimed at de‑escalating tensions along the disputed border and addressing broader security concerns, have been closely watched by regional actors and international observers. Previous rounds have produced limited agreements on humanitarian access and the reduction of cross‑border incidents, but core issues such as the presence of armed groups and border demarcation remain unresolved. The postponement is unlikely to alter the overall trajectory of the mediation effort, though it may extend the timeline for achieving a comprehensive settlement.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Crypto billionaire donates $49 million to Reform UK, total pledges hit $97 million
content:
Two recent contributions have lifted the amount pledged to Reform to a cumulative $97 million since Friday, according to the organization’s latest fundraising report. The donations, made by undisclosed benefactors, were the latest in a series of pledges that have accelerated the campaign’s cash intake over the past 48 hours.

The surge in contributions follows an intensive outreach effort by Reform, which began a week ago and has attracted a broad base of supporters. With the total now approaching the $100‑million mark, the organization indicated that the funds will be allocated toward upcoming operational initiatives and strategic projects. Fundraisers said the momentum is expected to continue as the campaign moves toward its next major milestone.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ebola reaches seventh province in DR Congo as government says cases are declining
content:
The Democratic Republic of Congo’s ongoing Ebola outbreak has expanded to a seventh province after health officials confirmed that a man who had traveled through Rwanda and Uganda tested positive for the virus. The patient, who was initially treated in a border clinic before being transferred to a treatment center in the capital, is believed to have contracted the disease in the eastern region before moving westward, prompting authorities to trace his movements across three countries and issue alerts to neighboring health facilities.

The newly affected province joins the six previously confirmed zones—North Kivu, Ituri, South Kivu, Tanganyika, Haut-Uélé and Bas-Uélé—bringing the total to 1.2 million residents at risk. The Ministry of Health, in coordination with the World Health Organization and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, has deployed rapid response teams, intensified contact tracing, and reinforced border screenings to curb further spread. Officials emphasized that the cross‑border transmission underscores the need for regional cooperation, and they pledged continued surveillance and vaccination campaigns as the outbreak enters its third month.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Fire at Chile nursing home kills 16 residents
content:
Ten individuals were evacuated from a private residence in Chile’s Araucanía region, located in the central part of the country, after local authorities responded to an emergency call. Emergency services, including the regional fire department and police, arrived on scene to secure the property and ensure the safety of the occupants, who were subsequently taken to a nearby shelter for temporary accommodation.

The evacuation was carried out without reported injuries, and officials are assessing the situation to determine the cause of the incident. Residents in the surrounding area were advised to remain vigilant while authorities complete their investigation and restore normal conditions to the neighborhood.
author: BBC World

title: Jeremy Thomas, Oscar-Winning Film Producer, Dies at 77
content:
British film producer David Puttnam, best known for his work on the Academy‑Award‑winning *The Last Emperor* and the critically acclaimed *Sexy Beast*, died on Tuesday at the age of 78.  The 1964‑born producer had a career spanning more than four decades, during which he collaborated with a wide range of international directors, from Bernardo Bertolucci to Ken Watanabe, and helped bring a diverse array of stories to global audiences.

Puttnam’s filmography includes a mix of historical epics, dramas and thrillers, and he was recognised for his ability to balance artistic ambition with commercial viability.  He earned an Academy Award for Best Picture for *The Last Emperor* (1987) and received a BAFTA Fellowship in 2010 for his contributions to the British film industry.  His work on *Sexy Beast* (2000) further cemented his reputation for supporting bold, unconventional projects that pushed genre boundaries.

Industry colleagues have described Puttnam as a visionary who championed cross‑cultural collaboration and nurtured emerging talent.  His legacy will be felt in the continued success of the films he produced and in the generations of filmmakers he inspired to pursue global storytelling.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Hull beat Chelsea 3-2, Belloumi double and João Pedro goal
content:
Hull City’s recent home fixture at Stamford Bridge saw the away supporters chant in jest about winning the league, a reminder that the club’s ambitions are firmly in place. The Tigers, who have remained unbeaten in their first four Premier League matches, finished third in the table after a hard‑fought 2‑1 victory over Chelsea. The win, achieved in front of a raucous crowd, underscored Hull’s growing confidence and their ability to challenge the traditional Big Six clubs.

The match was a tense affair, with Hull taking a 2‑1 lead at half‑time and creating several chances in the second period. Chelsea’s goalkeeper, Emiliano Martínez, made two crucial saves to keep the scoreline level, but the team struggled to convert opportunities. Early in the game, Morgan Rogers gave the visitors an initial advantage, only for Hull to level the score and then take the lead with a quick double from Mohamed Belloumi. The ease with which the advantage was turned over prompted Xabi Alonso to criticize his side for being “soft” when not in possession, a comment that highlighted the defensive lapses that cost Chelsea the match.

With the result, Hull City have cemented their position as a serious contender in the Premier League, proving they can compete against top‑flight opposition. Their unbeaten start and recent victory over Chelsea demonstrate that the club’s resurgence is not a fleeting phenomenon, and they will likely continue to challenge for higher league positions as the season progresses.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Enric Mas Clinches Vuelta a España Title on Penultimate Stage
content:
Enric Mas has secured overall victory in the Vuelta a España, becoming the first Spanish rider to win the race since Alberto Contador 12 years ago. The 31‑year‑old Movistar rider’s triumph came after a decisive performance on the penultimate stage, where he maintained his lead and sealed the red jersey for himself.

The 186‑km stage ran up the sun‑baked slopes of the Sierra Nevada, a brutal test that saw Mas hold his ground in a small group that included Primož Roglic, Félix Gall and Richard Carapaz. The quartet were the only men capable of threatening Mas’s advantage, yet he refused to crack, staying with the group and withstanding the harsh conditions to keep his overall lead intact.

With the final stage now complete, Mas’s victory cements his status as one of the sport’s top climbers and marks a historic moment for Spanish cycling, echoing the triumphs of past champions in the Vuelta’s storied history.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England defeat Australia 48-15 in WXV after second‑half surge
content:
England’s women’s rugby team secured a 48‑15 victory over Australia on Saturday, overturning a 15‑15 halftime deadlock to extend their unbeaten run. The win marked the first occasion in nearly six years that the Red Roses fell behind after the first 40 minutes of a test match, prompting a decisive second‑half surge that produced 43 unanswered points.

Australia, playing some of their strongest rugby since the 2023 World Cup quarter‑final exit, applied early pressure with solid attacking play and a physical defensive line that disrupted England’s front‑foot ball. Despite a handful of knock‑ons and handling errors that hampered the English attack in the first half, the Red Roses rallied after the break, with May Campbell igniting a flurry of seven tries that cemented the comeback. The comprehensive second‑half performance not only restored England’s dominance but also kept their winning streak alive heading into upcoming fixtures.
author: Guardian Sport

title: A star is born: Razaullah gives Pakistan fresh hopes despite England sweep | Andy Bull
content:
A 21‑year‑old fast bowler made a striking Test debut, turning a bleak summer for the touring side into a moment of bright possibility. In the opening over England’s batting faltered, losing two wickets before the crowd erupted in the first loud cries of “Pakistan, Zindabad.” The sudden shift in momentum gave the match a fleeting sense of contest that had been missing from the series.

The debutant’s performance, highlighted by a series of incisive deliveries, provided the tourists with a rare spark of excitement amid a largely unproductive campaign. While the overall series remained one-sided, the early wickets and the palpable energy at the ground suggested that the match could have unfolded differently, keeping spectators and players alike on edge.

In the end, however, the tourists were unable to sustain the early advantage, and the series concluded with the home side maintaining a comfortable lead. The debutant’s impressive showing remains a bright note in an otherwise disappointing summer for the touring team.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Tottenham Hotspur 0-0 Everton: Premier League – live
content:
The Premier League match between Tottenham Hotspur and Everton began at 5:30 pm BST, with both sides eager to secure a vital point in the run‑up to the season’s final stages. Tottenham’s early tempo saw the visitors settle quickly, with the ball repeatedly pinging around the edge of Everton’s penalty area as the Spurs looked to create chances.

A camera cut to a group of young supporters in the stands holding a sign that read “Please score a goal”, though it was unclear which side they were backing. The atmosphere was charged as Everton kicked off, with fans chanting “Peeeeeep!” and rallying behind their team as the match progressed.

The game remains live, with updates on scores, league tables and top scorers available for viewers. As the match continues, both clubs will be looking to capitalize on any opportunities to improve their positions in the Premier League standings.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Lando Norris Sees Win Chance at Spanish GP Despite McLaren's Speed Gap
content:
At the Spanish Grand Prix, McLaren drivers will be hampered by a car that lags behind the front‑running field, yet the team’s pole sitter, Lando Norris, still has a realistic shot at victory. The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya is known for its long straights and tight corners, a layout that historically limits overtaking opportunities and rewards a clean start and strong qualifying pace.

McLaren’s recent telemetry shows the car’s power unit and aerodynamic package are not yet on par with the dominant Mercedes and Red Bull machines. Nevertheless, Norris secured pole position with a blistering lap, giving him the advantage of clear air at the start and a better chance to control the race from the front. With the track’s limited passing spots, a disciplined drive and strategic pit stops will be crucial for Norris to maintain his lead against the faster rivals.

If Norris can keep the pressure on the backmarkers and avoid any on‑track incidents, the combination of a strong start and the track’s overtaking constraints could allow him to convert the pole into another win, adding to his growing tally of podiums for the season.
author: BBC Sport

title: Hull-Woad pairing under scrutiny as Europe seeks 14½ points in Solheim Cup
content:
Europe will need 14½ points to secure the Solheim Cup on Sunday, a target that has already sparked scrutiny of captain Anna Nordqvist’s decision to pair Charley Hull and Lottie Woad. The duo, both in the top 10 of the Women's World Golf Rankings, have yet to play together in a major team event, raising questions about their chemistry and how they will handle the pressure of a high‑stakes match.

The Cup, held at the Royal County Down Golf Club, has seen Europe hold a narrow advantage over the United States after the first two days. Hull and Woad’s individual strengths—Hull’s aggressive ball‑striking and Woad’s steadiness under pressure—could complement each other, but their lack of shared experience may prove costly in the tight, match‑play format. Nordqvist’s confidence in the pairing reflects her broader strategy of blending seasoned veterans with emerging talent, a gamble that could pay off if the pair quickly find rhythm.

If Europe fails to reach the 14½‑point threshold, the United States will claim victory, underscoring the importance of every point in this fiercely contested event. The outcome will also influence how captains approach pairings in future Solheim Cups, as the balance between experience and fresh combinations remains a pivotal factor in team success.
author: BBC Sport

title: Alonso Criticises Chelsea After 2-2 Draw with Hull City
content:
Chelsea’s home form suffered a setback on Saturday as the Blues were held to a 2‑2 draw by newly promoted Hull City at Stamford Bridge. The match, which saw both sides exchange goals in the first half, ended in a stalemate that left the Premier League leaders with a single point from a home fixture. Hull’s two goals came from a first‑half penalty and a late strike, while Chelsea’s equaliser was scored by a substitute who made an immediate impact.

The result has dampened the atmosphere at Stamford Bridge, where the club’s supporters were noticeably subdued compared to recent home fixtures. Analysts point to the defensive lapses that allowed Hull to capitalize on set‑pieces and the failure to maintain possession in the final minutes. Despite the draw, Chelsea’s manager praised the team’s resilience and highlighted the need to address the defensive issues before the next round of fixtures.

In the broader context of the Premier League campaign, the draw has left Chelsea a point behind the league leaders, tightening the race for the top spot. The club will look to regain momentum in their upcoming matches, while Hull City will celebrate their first-ever points haul at Stamford Bridge as they aim to consolidate their position in the top flight.
author: BBC Sport

title: Trump Plans Midterm Blitz, GOP Candidates Weigh Impact
content:
President Donald J. Trump is set to launch a mid‑term campaign blitz that could jeopardise Republican prospects in several hard‑to‑win races, according to polling data released this week.  His approval rating has fallen sharply in the run‑up to November, a trend that analysts say could dampen enthusiasm among voters who might otherwise lean toward Republican candidates.  The former president’s visit to battleground North Carolina is part of a broader strategy to shore up the GOP’s hold on the state’s Senate seat.

The campaign will take place on Wednesday, when Trump will travel to North Carolina to campaign alongside Senate nominee Michael Whatley.  Whatley, who is running to retain the seat for the Republicans, has been facing a tough reelection bid against a well‑funded Democratic challenger.  Trump’s presence is intended to energise the base and bring additional media attention to the race, but observers warn that his declining popularity could backfire, especially in a state that has shown signs of shifting toward the center in recent elections.

If the strategy succeeds, it could provide a much‑needed boost to the Republican ticket in North Carolina and other swing districts.  However, the risk remains that Trump’s polarising image and falling approval may alienate moderate voters, potentially costing the GOP seats it seeks to defend.  The outcome of the North Carolina Senate race will likely serve as a bellwether for the broader impact of Trump’s mid‑term push on the Republican Party’s electoral fortunes.
author: The Hill

title: JD Vance Praised for Loyalty and Mature Decision-Making on International Stage
content:
On Thursday, during a high‑profile summit in Geneva, Ance made a decisive move that set him apart from his peers. Choosing loyalty to his long‑term allies over short‑term political gains, he vetoed a proposed amendment that would have shifted the alliance’s stance on a contentious trade dispute. The decision, announced in a brief statement, underscored his commitment to a consistent foreign‑policy framework.

The vote came after months of negotiations between the bloc’s member states and a major global power. While most delegates pushed for a compromise that would have appeased domestic critics, Ance argued that the amendment would erode the alliance’s credibility and undermine its strategic objectives. His stance earned him the description of one of the few “adults in the room” on the international stage, a phrase used by several diplomats to highlight his measured, principled approach.

The move is expected to reinforce the alliance’s long‑term credibility and may influence future diplomatic negotiations. Observers note that Ance’s willingness to prioritize loyalty over expediency could set a precedent for other leaders, encouraging a shift toward more principled decision‑making in international affairs.
author: The Hill

title: Surrogate Fled to Texas Over Abortion Request, Seeks Supreme Court Intervention
content:
A surrogate who fled to Texas after the unborn child’s biological parents requested she terminate the pregnancy has asked the U.S. Supreme Court to intervene in a custody dispute that has drawn national attention. McKenna West, the surrogate, filed an emergency application Wednesday seeking a temporary halt to the proceedings that would allow the parents to claim custody and potentially force an abortion. The case has already attracted the attention of Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, who has publicly criticized the surrogate’s decision and urged state authorities to support the parents’ request.

West’s petition argues that the court order currently in place violates her rights as a surrogate and threatens the unborn child’s well‑being. She requests that the Supreme Court issue a stay on any lower‑court orders that would compel the termination of the pregnancy or transfer custody to the biological parents. Paxton’s intervention has amplified the case, prompting state officials to consider whether Texas law should override the surrogate’s contractual and constitutional protections.

If the Supreme Court grants the emergency stay, the case would likely be sent back to a lower court for a more detailed hearing. The outcome could set a precedent for future surrogacy agreements and the extent to which parents can influence the medical decisions of a surrogate, underscoring the ongoing legal and ethical tensions surrounding reproductive rights in the United States.
author: The Hill

title: Immigrant caregiver visa lapses threaten senior care in the U.S.
content:
**Lapsed Visas Strip Residents of Essential Support**

When a visa or protection status expires, residents often lose the person who best understands their daily routines, medical care needs, and potential risks. The sudden loss of a familiar support figure can leave individuals vulnerable to health complications, unsafe living conditions, and administrative confusion, experts say. This phenomenon is particularly acute among asylum seekers and long‑term migrants who rely on community networks to navigate complex legal and social systems.

The issue has drawn attention from both advocacy groups and policymakers. Human‑rights organizations argue that the abrupt termination of support structures can lead to a cascade of problems, including missed medical appointments, exposure to exploitation, and heightened anxiety. In response, some jurisdictions have introduced temporary bridging visas and community outreach programs to mitigate the disruption, but gaps remain in ensuring continuous care and protection for those whose status has lapsed.

Ultimately, the loss of a trusted support person underscores the broader challenges of maintaining continuity of care for residents with precarious legal status. Addressing these gaps will require coordinated efforts between immigration authorities, health services, and community organizations to provide stable, ongoing assistance to those most at risk.
author: The Hill

title: Anthropic CEO urges slowdown in AI development for safety
content:
Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei announced on Saturday that the pace of artificial‑intelligence development should be slowed to give regulators and industry players time to install adequate risk‑mitigation safeguards. In a blog post, Amodei wrote that “we must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models,” adding that progress would still appear rapid but would need to be guided by prudent use of safety measures.

The statement follows a broader industry debate over the speed at which increasingly powerful language models are released. Amodei emphasized that the ability to deploy new features quickly must be balanced against the potential for misuse or unintended consequences, urging a more measured approach to scaling AI capabilities. He called for coordinated efforts between companies, policymakers, and researchers to establish standards and oversight mechanisms that can keep pace with technical advances.

While Anthropic has continued to push forward with new model releases, the CEO’s call signals a shift toward a more cautious development trajectory. The company’s emphasis on safety aligns with growing calls for regulatory frameworks that can adapt to the rapid evolution of AI technology, aiming to ensure that progress in the field does not outstrip the safeguards designed to protect users and society at large.
author: The Hill

title: US Faces 187,000 Physician Shortage by Mid-2030s
content:
The United States is expected to face a shortage of roughly 187,000 physicians by the mid‑2030s, according to recent projections that link the gap to a federal residency funding cap set in 1997. The cap limits the number of residency positions that can be funded by Medicare, effectively constraining the growth of the medical workforce even as demand for primary and specialty care continues to rise.

Health‑policy analysts point to the aging population, increasing prevalence of chronic diseases, and the expansion of health‑care access under the Affordable Care Act as key drivers of the projected shortfall. The 1997 cap, originally intended to control federal spending, has become a bottleneck that restricts the number of new doctors entering the field, while state‑level initiatives to increase residency slots have been unevenly implemented.

If current trends persist, the shortage could strain hospitals, delay patient care, and elevate health‑care costs. Policymakers are debating reforms to the residency funding structure, including potential increases in Medicare reimbursement for residency programs, to address the looming deficit and ensure adequate medical staffing across the country.
author: The Hill

title: Trump Adviser Cautiously Optimistic About GOP Holding Congress
content:
A senior adviser to former President Donald Trump has expressed cautious optimism that the Republican Party can retain control of Congress in the upcoming November elections, even as the party faces significant headwinds and the former president’s approval ratings continue to decline. James Blair, who has served as a key strategist for Trump, told NBC News that while he would not predict exact seat counts, he believes the GOP still has a viable path to maintaining its majorities in both chambers.

Blair noted that the political landscape is challenging, citing a broader national swing toward Democrats in recent polls and the president’s diminishing popularity among voters. Despite these factors, he emphasized that the Republican base remains energized and that strategic campaigning could offset the negative trends. The adviser highlighted the importance of turnout and targeted messaging in key battleground districts as critical to the party’s success.

As the election cycle progresses, the Republican leadership will likely focus on mobilizing supporters and addressing the issues that have eroded Trump’s approval. While Blair’s remarks signal a hopeful outlook for the GOP, the final outcome will depend on voter turnout, campaign effectiveness, and the evolving political climate in the months leading up to the vote.
author: The Hill

title: First Alien Terrorist Removal Court Case: US Resident Deported to Afghanistan
content:
Nazira Haji Zada, a lawful permanent resident of the United States, has admitted to being an “alien terrorist,” a plea that will be heard in the newly established Alien Terrorist Removal Court. The court, created under the 2024 National Security and Immigration Reform Act, is the first of its kind to adjudicate cases involving non‑citizens who are alleged to pose a national‑security threat while holding lawful permanent resident status. Zada’s admission marks the inaugural proceeding in this specialized tribunal.

The court’s mandate is to expedite removal proceedings for individuals deemed to be engaged in terrorist activities or who have ties to foreign terrorist organizations. In Zada’s case, prosecutors allege that she provided logistical support to a designated extremist group, a claim she has now acknowledged. The proceedings will determine whether she will be deported, face criminal charges, or be subjected to other security measures, and will set a precedent for how the court handles future cases involving lawful permanent residents.

If the court upholds the removal order, Zada will be expelled from the United States and barred from reentry. The decision will also signal the government’s willingness to apply the new legal framework to high‑profile security threats, potentially influencing the treatment of other permanent residents suspected of terrorism.
author: NPR Politics

title: ADHD and Autism Diagnoses Shift Toward General Population Traits Over Last Decade
content:
A recent study conducted by the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal) in collaboration with Aarhus University has revealed that Danish children and adolescents diagnosed with attention‑deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) or autism spectrum disorder (ASD) today exhibit characteristics that are increasingly similar to their peers in the general population. The research, which compared contemporary diagnostic cohorts with those identified a decade earlier, found that the present group shows fewer distinct clinical features and a broader range of symptom severity.

The investigators highlighted that the shift toward a more inclusive diagnostic profile may reflect changes in diagnostic criteria, heightened public awareness, and evolving clinical practices over the past ten years. As a result, children who receive an ADHD or ASD diagnosis now tend to have milder symptomatology and greater overlap with typical developmental trajectories than those diagnosed in the previous decade.

These findings suggest that health services and educational systems will need to adapt to a more heterogeneous patient population, ensuring that support and intervention strategies remain responsive to the full spectrum of needs within the ADHD and ASD communities.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Which? Calls Jack Mackerel Sale Skimpflation
content:
Consumer watchdog Which? has warned that the growing popularity of jack mackerel in supermarkets is a clear case of “skimpflation,” a term used to describe the substitution of lower‑quality, cheaper products for more expensive ones. The group argues that jack mackerel, which is less nutrient‑dense than traditional salmon or cod, is being marketed as a budget alternative while still carrying a premium price tag.

The campaign notes that jack mackerel contains lower levels of omega‑3 fatty acids and protein compared with its pricier counterparts, yet retailers often price it similarly to higher‑grade fish. Which? cites data showing a steady rise in the sale of this species over the past year, coinciding with broader food‑price inflation. The organization calls on consumers to be aware of the nutritional trade‑off and urges retailers to provide clearer labeling.

Which? concludes that the shift toward jack mackerel reflects a broader trend of cost‑cutting in the food industry, where companies replace higher‑quality ingredients with cheaper substitutes. The group urges both shoppers and suppliers to consider the long‑term health implications of such substitutions while monitoring price changes in the seafood market.
author: BBC Business

title: Cell stress implicated in salivary gland failure causing dry mouth in radiation, Sjögren’s, diabetes, and aging
content:
Reduced saliva production, known medically as xerostomia, poses a serious health concern for several vulnerable groups, including cancer patients receiving head and neck radiation therapy, individuals with Sjögren’s syndrome, people with diabetes, and older adults. In these populations, the condition extends beyond mere discomfort; it interferes with essential oral functions and can significantly diminish overall well‑being.

The lack of adequate saliva hampers eating, speaking, and swallowing, alters taste perception, and creates an environment conducive to dental cavities and oral infections. These complications can lead to nutritional deficiencies, increased medical expenses, and a heightened need for dental and medical interventions, underscoring the importance of early identification and management of xerostomia in at‑risk patients.
author: Phys.org

title: Southern Ocean May Become Carbon Source With Climate Mitigation
content:
Scientists warn that the global effort to cap warming at 1.5 °C above pre‑industrial levels, which relies on achieving net‑zero emissions and actively removing carbon dioxide (CO₂) from the atmosphere, could have an unforeseen side effect. A new study published in *Science Advances* used climate simulations to show that the Southern Ocean surrounding Antarctica may shift from being a significant carbon sink to becoming a net source of CO₂ as atmospheric concentrations fall.

The research highlights the complex feedbacks in the Earth system. While reducing CO₂ is essential to limit extreme weather, sea‑level rise, ecosystem loss and the risk of triggering irreversible climate tipping points, the Southern Ocean’s response could undermine some of those gains. The model suggests that changes in ocean circulation, temperature, and biological activity could release stored carbon, potentially offsetting the benefits of emissions reductions and carbon‑removal technologies.

These findings underscore the need for continuous monitoring of oceanic carbon fluxes and for climate policy to incorporate adaptive strategies that account for such nonlinear feedbacks. Ensuring that mitigation pathways remain effective will require a deeper understanding of regional climate dynamics and the development of flexible, evidence‑based approaches to carbon management.
author: Phys.org

title: Central North Amazon Sees Fastest Rise in Extreme Heat and Water Stress
content:
Recent research has shifted the focus of climate‑change vulnerability assessments to the central north Amazon, an area previously thought to be less impacted than its southern counterparts. The region, characterized by dense tropical forest, extensive natural savannas, and large Indigenous territories, is now identified as experiencing accelerated temperature rises, altered rainfall patterns, and increased frequency of extreme weather events. These changes threaten the ecological integrity of the forest and the cultural and subsistence practices of the Indigenous communities that depend on it.

The updated findings stem from high‑resolution climate models and satellite observations that reveal a pronounced warming trend of up to 1.5 °C over the past two decades, coupled with a shift in precipitation that favors drier conditions during the dry season. Deforestation rates, while lower than in the southern Amazon, have intensified in key corridors, exacerbating the region’s susceptibility to forest fires and loss of biodiversity. Indigenous land managers report heightened fire risk and reduced fish stocks, underscoring the intertwined ecological and socio‑cultural impacts of these climatic shifts.

These insights call for a recalibration of conservation priorities and climate adaptation strategies in the central north Amazon. Protecting forest cover, supporting Indigenous stewardship, and implementing fire‑management protocols are essential to mitigate the region’s emerging climate vulnerabilities and preserve its ecological and cultural heritage.
author: Phys.org

title: Waymo pulls over juvenile riders carrying ghost gun
content:
On September 12, 2026, Los Angeles County police arrested three juveniles after discovering a ghost gun in a Waymo autonomous vehicle that was being used as a rideshare service. The vehicle, operating in the city’s downtown corridor, was found to contain an unregistered, 3‑dollar “ghost” firearm that had been illegally assembled from a 3‑dollar gun kit. The juveniles, all under the age of 18, were charged with possession of an unregistered firearm and related offenses, and the case was referred to the county district attorney’s office for further action.

The incident prompted an immediate review of Waymo’s security protocols for its autonomous rideshare fleet. Waymo’s spokesperson stated that the company has implemented a multi‑layered safety system that includes vehicle‑level sensors, driver‑monitoring software, and real‑time traffic monitoring, but that the presence of a ghost gun indicates a lapse in the vehicle’s physical security measures. California law prohibits the possession of unregistered firearms, and the state’s recent legislation on ghost guns imposes strict penalties for the manufacturing and sale of such weapons. The discovery has raised concerns among regulators about the potential for illicit weapons to be introduced into autonomous vehicles, which are designed to operate without a human driver.

Waymo has pledged full cooperation with law enforcement and is conducting an internal audit of its vehicle security protocols. The Los Angeles Police Department is continuing its investigation to determine how the ghost gun entered the vehicle and whether other vehicles in the fleet may have been compromised. The case underscores the need for robust security measures in autonomous transportation systems and highlights the ongoing challenges of enforcing gun‑control laws in a rapidly evolving technology landscape.
author: Hacker News

title: Developer Promises to Keep SPICE Software Alive
content:
**GitHub Repository “vd_agent” Sparks Discussion on Hacker News**

A new Windows driver project, *vd_agent*, hosted on GitHub by user nefarius, has attracted attention from the tech community. The repository provides a lightweight driver that can be used to expose virtual devices to Windows applications, enabling developers to create custom hardware interfaces or extend system capabilities. The project was highlighted on Hacker News, where it received 51 points and 39 comments, indicating a moderate but engaged audience.

The codebase includes the driver’s source, installation scripts, and documentation on how to compile and load the module. It is distributed under the MIT license, allowing free use and modification. Users can employ *vd_agent* to create virtual serial ports, emulate USB devices, or provide a sandboxed environment for testing device drivers. The repository also contains example applications demonstrating the driver’s functionality, making it a practical starting point for developers interested in low‑level Windows programming.

The discussion on Hacker News centers on the driver’s potential for rapid prototyping and its implications for security testing. While some commenters praise its simplicity and open‑source nature, others raise concerns about stability and the need for thorough testing before deployment in production systems. Overall, the project demonstrates how community‑driven open‑source tools can accelerate innovation in system‑level development.

title: Intel 8087 floating‑point chip scale instruction microcode reverse‑engineered
content:
A recent post on RightO’s blog details a reverse‑engineering effort that exposes the microcode of the FScale processor, a niche architecture used in embedded systems. The author, using a combination of binary disassembly, symbolic execution, and custom tooling, was able to reconstruct the hidden microcode tables that govern the CPU’s instruction set. The write‑up walks readers through the methodology, the challenges of dealing with undocumented opcodes, and the implications of having a publicly available microcode map for the FScale family.

The project’s findings have drawn attention from the security community, as the microcode layer often contains critical control logic that can be targeted for firmware exploits or patched to fix hardware bugs. By revealing the internal state transitions and control signals, the reverse‑engineering work enables more precise debugging, potential firmware updates, and a better understanding of the processor’s performance characteristics. The discussion thread on Hacker News, which has accumulated 40 points and eight comments, highlights the technical interest and the practical value of the research for developers working with legacy or proprietary hardware.

In conclusion, the RightO blog post offers a comprehensive look at how to peel back the layers of a proprietary CPU’s microcode, providing a valuable resource for researchers and engineers. The community’s engagement on Hacker News underscores the relevance of this work in the broader context of hardware security and reverse engineering.

title: First Edit on OpenStreetMap: How to Use the JOSM Website Wizard
content:
High5apps has released a new open‑source plugin for JOSM, the popular editor used by OpenStreetMap contributors. The “Website Wizard” plugin, hosted on GitHub at https://high5apps.github.io/josm-plugin-website-wizard/, is designed to streamline the creation of web pages that display map data, allowing users to generate static sites directly from JOSM projects without manual coding.

The plugin was highlighted on Hacker News (post ID 49674050), where it accumulated 91 up‑votes and drew 31 comments from the community. Reviewers noted the tool’s ease of use and potential to broaden the reach of OpenStreetMap data by making it more accessible to web developers and non‑technical users alike. The GitHub repository includes documentation, example configurations, and a permissive license that encourages further contributions.

With its initial reception, the Website Wizard is poised to become a useful addition to the JOSM ecosystem, offering map editors a quick path from data to web presentation. The active discussion on Hacker News suggests that the plugin will likely see continued development and refinement as users share use cases and suggest enhancements.

title: Anthropic CEO Calls for Slowing AI Development
content:
Anthropic’s chief executive, Dario Amodei, has announced that the company will begin to slow the pace of its AI development and will grant third‑party evaluators, such as METR, broad access to its models. The move is intended to reinforce the company’s commitment to safety practices and to allow independent verification of its compliance with internal and external standards.

Amodei outlined a three‑step plan to “pace the frontier.” The first step, already underway, is the unilateral provision of model access to external reviewers. The second step calls for industry‑wide cooperation, likely involving government partners, to establish common safety benchmarks and oversight mechanisms. While the final step is not detailed in the brief, it is implied to involve further regulatory alignment and coordinated risk mitigation across the sector.

By opening its models to independent scrutiny, Anthropic aims to create a more transparent development cycle and to give regulators the information needed to assess potential risks. The company’s initiative reflects a growing trend among AI firms to prioritize safety and oversight as they scale up model capabilities. For more detail, see the full story on The Verge.

title: Sylvan Esso releases new album Ow &∞ and gears up for upcoming event
content:
Sylvan Esso – the electronic‑pop duo of Amelia Meath and Nick Sanborn – announced they will attend the upcoming Frutiger Aero Renfaire, a gathering that blends music, art and retro‑futurist culture. The appearance follows the release of their latest album, Ow &∞, which dropped on Friday and marks the most pronounced stylistic shift in the pair’s catalog to date. The group’s participation in the event was confirmed through a statement released by their publicist, noting that the duo will perform a set featuring selections from the new record alongside earlier material.

Since their debut in 2014 with the self‑titled album and the single “Hey Mami,” Sylvan Esso has issued a series of critically acclaimed releases, including the texturally sparse Free Love (2020) and the rhythm‑driven, glitch‑inflected No Rules Sandy (2022). Their evolving sound has consistently retained the distinctive blend of melodic songwriting and electronic production that defines their work. Ow &∞ expands this foundation with bolder arrangements and experimental tones, signaling a continued commitment to artistic reinvention. The Verge’s full coverage provides additional insight into the album’s composition and the duo’s upcoming plans.

title: Silicon Valley executives skeptical of recent AI danger warnings
content:
Recent high‑profile warnings about the potential risks of artificial intelligence have sparked a notable degree of scepticism among corporate leaders and venture‑capital investors. Prominent voices—including former government officials, academic researchers, and industry watchdogs—have highlighted concerns ranging from algorithmic bias and privacy breaches to the possibility of autonomous systems acting beyond human control. Their statements have been amplified through media outlets and policy briefings, prompting calls for tighter regulation and more rigorous safety testing before wider deployment.

Executives at leading technology firms and investors in AI‑focused startups, however, have largely questioned the immediacy and severity of these threats. In recent earnings calls and industry conferences, CEOs emphasized ongoing internal risk‑assessment frameworks and the economic benefits of accelerated AI adoption, while venture capitalists cited robust market demand and competitive pressures as drivers for continued funding. The divergence underscores a broader debate over how to balance innovation with precaution, a discussion that is expected to shape forthcoming regulatory proposals and investment strategies.
author: BBC Technology

title: Israel installs “yellow line” markers near Gaza City homes
content:
Ola Ishtiwi is pictured seated with her children amid the rubble of her former home in the Al‑Tuffah neighbourhood of eastern Gaza City, just metres from a row of painted cement blocks that Israeli forces have installed to delineate the so‑called “yellow line.” The line, marked in bright yellow, is intended by the Israeli military to indicate the boundary of an area slated for demolition or restricted access as part of ongoing operations in the densely populated sector.

The “yellow line” has been introduced in the wake of intensified fighting between Israeli forces and Hamas, with authorities asserting that the demarcation is meant to separate combat zones from civilian areas and to facilitate the clearance of structures deemed to pose security risks. Residents, however, report that the markings have led to the displacement of families and the loss of housing, as exemplified by Ishtiwi’s situation. Humanitarian agencies have warned that the rapid establishment of such zones, without clear communication or adequate compensation, could exacerbate the already dire living conditions in Gaza. The scene underscores the broader challenges faced by civilians caught in the conflict’s shifting frontlines.
author: UN News

title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak exceeds 7,000 cases with 3,400 deaths
content:
Kinshasa — The Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ministry of Health announced on Tuesday that a rare outbreak of the Bundibugyo virus, a member of the ebolavirus family first identified in Uganda in 2007, was detected in mid‑May. Since the virus’s emergence, official figures indicate that nearly 3,400 people have died, making it one of the deadliest health crises the country has faced in recent years.

Health officials and World Health Organization teams have deployed rapid‑response units to the affected provinces, establishing treatment centers, conducting contact tracing, and distributing experimental vaccines under emergency protocols. The Ministry of Health warned that the virus spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids of infected individuals and stressed that limited laboratory capacity and ongoing conflict in remote areas hinder containment efforts. International partners are providing personal protective equipment, diagnostic kits, and logistical support as authorities continue to monitor the outbreak and urge communities to report symptoms promptly.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pakistan and Turkey may intervene in Yemen if Saudi Arabia requests, direct involvement unlikely
content:
Saudi Arabia has signaled that it may call on its regional partners, Pakistan and Turkey, for support in the ongoing conflict in Yemen, though both countries have indicated that any assistance would be limited to indirect measures rather than direct military engagement. The prospect of a Saudi request comes amid a protracted war that began in 2015 when a Saudi‑led coalition intervened to restore the internationally recognized government against Houthi rebels, a conflict that has resulted in a severe humanitarian crisis and drawn in various external actors.

Both Islamabad and Ankara have underscored their willingness to respond to a Saudi appeal, emphasizing diplomatic, logistical or advisory roles while stopping short of committing combat troops to Yemen’s battlefields. Analysts note that Pakistan’s historical ties with Saudi Arabia and Turkey’s strategic interests in the Red Sea region shape this cautious stance, but the complexities of the Yemen war and domestic considerations make full-scale involvement unlikely. The conditional support reflects broader regional calculations, suggesting that any future assistance will be measured and indirect rather than a direct entry into the Yemeni conflict.

title: Chelsea draw with Hull, Liverpool held by Fulham and Villa stay winless
content:
Hull City came close to securing a Premier League victory at Stamford Bridge, only to settle for a 1‑1 draw after conceding an equaliser late in the second half. The hosts, Chelsea, dominated possession but were unable to convert their chances, while Hull’s resilience earned them a valuable point that lifts them a place up the table and narrows the gap to the relegation zone. In other fixtures, Liverpool were held to a goalless stalemate at Anfield, and Fulham likewise finished 0‑0 away, each side missing opportunities to claim all three points. Aston Villa suffered another defeat, losing 2‑0 on the road, extending their winless run and leaving them entrenched in the lower tier of the standings.

The results leave Hull poised to continue their push for safety, while Liverpool and Fulham remain steady but unremarkable in the mid‑table, each having failed to add to their point totals. Villa’s consecutive loss underscores the challenges the club faces as it strives to climb out of the relegation battle. The outcomes will shape the upcoming weekend’s fixtures, with teams looking to capitalize on the shifting dynamics across the league.

title: Greek couple births child from 22‑year‑old frozen embryo
content:
A couple from Athens announced the birth of their son on Tuesday, marking the first successful use in Greece of an embryo that had been cryopreserved for 22 years. The child was conceived through in‑vitro fertilisation (IVF) after the couple’s stored embryo, created in 2002, was thawed and implanted at a private fertility clinic in the capital.

The embryo was originally frozen at the clinic’s laboratory following a standard IVF cycle in which the couple, then in their early thirties, produced multiple embryos. After deciding not to proceed with a transfer at that time, one embryo was placed in long‑term storage. In 2024, the couple, now in their mid‑fifties, requested its use; the clinic reported that the thawed embryo survived the process, resulting in a successful pregnancy and a healthy full‑term delivery. The case surpasses the previous European record of a 21‑year‑old frozen embryo that led to a live birth and aligns with recent data showing that embryos can remain viable for decades when stored under optimal conditions. Greek legislation permits embryo storage for up to 20 years, but the clinic obtained a special extension in accordance with national health regulations.

The birth underscores the durability of modern cryopreservation techniques and offers renewed hope for individuals and couples who have previously stored embryos. Medical experts note that the outcome may encourage reassessment of storage limits and highlight the importance of clear consent procedures for long‑term embryo preservation.

title: Man arrested in connection with murder of Tasia Fortune found hanging from tree
content:
Police announced the arrest of a man suspected of killing Tasia Fortune, a Black woman whose body was discovered hanging from a tree. Authorities said the arrest follows a multi‑day investigation after the victim was found in a residential area, prompting a homicide inquiry. The suspect was taken into custody without incident, and detectives are reviewing forensic evidence and witness statements to build a case.

Law enforcement officials have not released the suspect’s identity or motive, emphasizing that the investigation remains ongoing. They urged anyone with additional information to contact the police department. The department reiterated its commitment to a thorough investigation and to bringing justice for Fortune and her family.

title: India and Sri Lanka to contest Women's T20 Asia Cup 2026 final in Dubai
content:
India are set to contest the final of the Dubai International Cricket Championship on Sunday, aiming to secure a record‑extending eighth title. The Indian side, which has previously lifted the trophy seven times, will face defending champions Sri Lanka, who claimed the championship in the previous edition. The match will be played at the Dubai International Stadium, with both teams having progressed through group stages and knockout rounds to reach the showdown.

Sri Lanka entered the final as the reigning champions after a narrow victory in last year’s tournament, while India’s campaign has been marked by dominant performances from both its batting and bowling units. The contest will determine whether India can extend its record tally of titles or if Sri Lanka will retain the crown for a second consecutive year. The outcome will be decided on the field on Sunday, with the winner earning the prestigious Dubai International Cricket Championship trophy.

title: Trump administration finds it harder to promote Iran war
content:
Washington’s effort to build public backing for a direct military conflict with Iran has grown increasingly difficult for the Trump administration, which has faced mounting skepticism from both the American electorate and congressional leaders. Since the 2018 decision to withdraw the United States from the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action and re‑impose sweeping sanctions, the administration has pursued a strategy of heightened pressure, including the designation of Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps units as terrorist organizations and the expansion of sanctions targeting Iran’s oil exports and financial networks. Despite these moves, polls conducted throughout 2019 and 2020 consistently showed a majority of Americans opposed to further escalation, and key members of Congress from both parties expressed concerns about the legal and strategic ramifications of a full‑scale war.

The administration’s challenges have been compounded by diplomatic setbacks and regional complexities, such as the ongoing proxy confrontations in Iraq, Syria, and Yemen, which have blurred the lines between limited strikes and broader hostilities. Efforts to rally allies in Europe and the Middle East have encountered hesitancy, as several NATO partners have called for restraint and emphasized the importance of a negotiated settlement. As the administration continued to promote a narrative of confronting Iran’s malign activities, the lack of clear consensus and the potential for a costly, protracted conflict have made the prospect of selling a war on Iran increasingly untenable.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Tooro kingdom names TV news presenter as new monarch after King Oyo's burial
content:
A television news presenter has been announced as the new monarch of the traditional Tooro Kingdom in western Uganda, following the death of the late king. The kingdom’s council of elders, known as the Abakama, issued a statement naming the broadcaster as the successor, citing customary procedures that allow the council to appoint a ruler when a clear line of succession is not established.

The late king’s family, however, disputes the appointment, asserting that the monarch had privately designated a different heir before his death. Family representatives have called for a review of the council’s decision, emphasizing that the late king’s wishes should be honored according to both cultural norms and the kingdom’s own succession guidelines. The disagreement has prompted calls for mediation by senior traditional leaders and has raised questions about the balance between council authority and the expressed preferences of a reigning monarch.

The Tooro Kingdom, which maintains a ceremonial role within Uganda’s constitutional framework, is expected to resolve the succession issue through its established dispute‑resolution mechanisms. Until a consensus is reached, the council’s appointment remains provisional, and the kingdom’s leadership will continue to operate under interim arrangements.

title: 14 Classic Star Trek Spaceships Ranked
content:
Nova Aerospace announced today the upcoming launch of its new deep‑space vessel, the Nova‑1, slated for a 2027 launch from Cape Canaveral’s Space Launch Complex 41. The spacecraft is being positioned as a versatile platform for crewed and robotic missions beyond low Earth orbit, with a primary target of a Mars fly‑by in the early 2030s. The company highlighted the vessel’s modular design, high‑efficiency ion propulsion system, and advanced radiation shielding as key innovations that aim to extend human presence farther into the solar system.

In a statement released alongside the announcement, Nova Aerospace CEO Elena Martinez emphasized the bold vision behind the project: “If you’re going to boldly go where no one has gone before, you may as well do it in a kick‑ass spaceship.” The quote underscores the company’s commitment to combining cutting‑edge technology with robust safety protocols. Nova‑1 will carry a crew of four and a suite of scientific instruments, and its development has involved partnerships with NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory and the European Space Agency.

The launch of Nova‑1 is expected to mark a significant milestone in commercial space exploration, potentially paving the way for future crewed missions to Mars and beyond. As the aerospace industry continues to expand its reach, Nova Aerospace’s entry into deep‑space travel represents a notable addition to the growing roster of private ventures aiming to extend humanity’s frontier.

title: This Week in Space Podcast Episode 227 Features Michael Okuda
content:
This Week in Space’s 227th episode spotlighted the creative force behind the iconic Star Trek aesthetic. Host Rod Pyle and co‑host Tariq Malik welcomed Michael Okuda—designer, writer, and longtime contributor to the franchise’s visual and narrative language—to discuss his career and the evolution of the series’ look and feel. Okuda, who has worked on every major Star Trek production since the 1970s, shared insights into the collaborative process that shaped the franchise’s distinctive style, from set design to costume and visual effects.

The conversation delved into Okuda’s partnership with his wife, who has also played a pivotal role in the series’ development, as well as the broader team of artists and technicians who bring the Star Trek universe to life. Pyle and Malik explored how the show’s visual identity has adapted to changing technology while maintaining continuity across decades of storytelling. The episode offered listeners a behind‑the‑scenes look at the creative minds that have kept the franchise’s aesthetic both recognizable and fresh for new and longtime fans alike.

title: Mae Jemison Becomes First Black Woman in Space
content:
On September 12, 1992, NASA astronaut Mae Jemison launched aboard the Space Shuttle *Endeavour* and became the first African‑American woman to travel into space. The flight, part of the STS‑47 mission, carried a scientific payload that included experiments in microgravity and a cultural exchange with the Soviet Union.

Jemison’s selection and success followed years of rigorous training and a career that spanned medical school, the U.S. Army, and the National Guard. Her presence aboard *Endeavour* challenged long‑standing stereotypes in both the aerospace and medical fields, underscoring NASA’s commitment to diversity and providing a visible role model for students of color and women pursuing STEM careers. The mission also highlighted the growing international cooperation in space exploration during the post‑Cold War era.

The historic flight had lasting effects on the scientific community and the public. It broadened the perception of who could be an astronaut, encouraged increased participation of underrepresented groups in space programs, and reinforced the idea that talent and dedication, rather than race or gender, are the true qualifications for space exploration.
author: Space.com

title: President Trump proposes U.S. Space Academy in executive order
content:
President Donald Trump signed an executive order this week establishing a United States Space Academy, a federal initiative intended to develop a pipeline of skilled professionals for the nation’s expanding civil and defense space programs. The order calls for the academy to provide interdisciplinary education in aerospace engineering, satellite operations, space law, and related fields, and to coordinate with existing agencies such as NASA, the Department of Defense, and the Federal Aviation Administration.

A space policy expert has identified a series of unanswered questions and potential challenges associated with the academy’s implementation. Concerns include the criteria for curriculum development and accreditation, the mechanisms for funding and resource allocation, and the degree of overlap with current university and military training programs. The expert also highlighted the need for clear governance structures, transparent admission standards, and a strategy to ensure the academy’s output aligns with both civilian and national security priorities without creating redundant capabilities.

The administration has indicated that interagency working groups will address these issues as the academy moves toward operational status, with a projected launch date in the next fiscal year. Congressional oversight and potential legislative action are expected to shape the final framework, while stakeholders await further details on budgetary commitments and partnership models.

title: Look Mum No Computer Still Gets Street Attention After Eurovision
content:
The frontman of the German pop trio Eins, Zwei, Drei, who represented Germany at the 2023 Eurovision Song Contest with the single “Stardust,” said in a recent interview that he is still being approached by fans on the street. The group’s performance, which finished in the top ten, has kept their name in the public eye long after the contest’s conclusion.

During a conversation with a local news outlet, the musician explained that he now routinely encounters people who recognize him from the Eurovision broadcast. He noted that fans often ask for autographs, photos, or simply to chat about the performance. The interview highlighted that the trio’s distinctive blend of pop and electronic music, combined with their memorable stage presence, has cultivated a dedicated following that extends beyond the contest’s immediate audience.

The musician’s experience underscores the lasting influence of Eurovision on participating artists. While the competition’s broadcast ends after the final night, the exposure continues to generate public interest and engagement for the performers, as evidenced by the ongoing street encounters reported by the frontman.

title: Dias names Maresca as ideal candidate for Man City role
content:
Manchester City defender Ruben Dias told BBC Sport’s Kelly Somers that the club is undergoing a period of transition following the departure of long‑time manager Pep Guardiola. Dias said the team is focused on maintaining the high standards set during Guardiola’s tenure while adapting to a new leadership structure that will see a fresh coaching philosophy and tactical approach.

According to Dias, the club’s priority is to preserve the winning culture that has defined City’s recent success, but he acknowledged that the squad will need to adjust to the expectations and systems introduced by the incoming management. He added that the players are committed to supporting the new regime and that the club’s infrastructure remains strong, with a clear emphasis on continuity in training and player development.

In closing, Dias expressed confidence that the club’s collective experience and professionalism will help it navigate the changes. He reiterated that the focus remains on performance on the pitch and on maintaining the club’s competitive edge in domestic and European competitions.

title: Saffie Osborne Becomes First Female Jockey to Win British Classic
content:
Saffie Osborne made history on Sunday when she rode Highwayman to victory in the St Leger at Doncaster, becoming the first female jockey to win a British Classic Flat race. The 26‑year‑old, who has been riding professionally since 2017, guided the 3‑year‑old colt to a decisive win in a field that included several top contenders.

The St Leger, the final leg of the five‑race British Classics, is a test of stamina over one mile, five furlongs and 110 yards. Osborne’s ride was marked by a well‑timed move in the final furlong, allowing Highwayman to pull away from the leaders and secure a comfortable margin. The victory not only cements Osborne’s place in racing history but also highlights the growing presence of female jockeys in the sport’s most prestigious events.

Osborne’s achievement is expected to inspire a new generation of riders and may prompt further discussion about gender diversity within professional horse racing. The win underscores the increasing competitiveness of female jockeys on the world’s biggest tracks and sets a new benchmark for future British Classic races.
author: BBC Sport

title: England dominate second half to beat Australia in WXV opener
content:
England dominated the second half to comfortably defeat Australia in the opening match of the new WXV Global Series, held at CorpAcq Stadium. The England squad displayed a clear tactical advantage, outscoring the Australian side after halftime and securing a decisive victory that set an early tone for the tournament.

The match, part of the inaugural WXV Global Series, saw England’s forwards and midfielders maintain pressure, while the defense successfully neutralised Australia’s attacking threats. The game’s outcome reflects England’s preparation and depth, while Australia’s performance highlighted areas for improvement as they look to regroup for the next fixtures.

With this win, England takes an early lead in the series, positioning themselves as strong contenders for the title. Australia will aim to adjust their strategy in upcoming games to remain competitive in the tournament’s remaining stages.

title: Norris Secures McLaren Pole at Spanish GP
content:
Lando Norris secured a remarkable pole position for McLaren at the Spanish Grand Prix, outpacing Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli and Red Bull’s Max Verstappen. The Austrian circuit saw Norris clock the fastest lap in qualifying, giving the British team a strong start to the weekend and a rare opportunity to challenge the dominant front‑row pair.

The performance came after a tight session where the Mercedes and Red Bull drivers posted competitive times, yet Norris’s lap was the quickest by a noticeable margin. The result not only boosts McLaren’s confidence ahead of the race but also highlights the team’s continued progress in car development and driver skill.

With the pole advantage, McLaren will aim to convert the position into a podium finish, while the Mercedes and Red Bull squads will look to recover lost time during the race. The outcome sets the stage for a competitive showdown in the Spanish Grand Prix’s opening laps.

title: England's Test Summer: September vs June
content:
England’s performance in September has sparked debate about whether the national side is stronger at the end of the summer than it was in June. BBC cricket correspondent Stephan Shemilt weighed in on the matter, noting that the team’s form has fluctuated throughout the Test season and that the timing of matches can influence outcomes. He highlighted that the September fixtures, played on pitches that tend to deteriorate, often reveal a team’s resilience and adaptability.

Shemilt outlined several positives from the Test summer, including the depth of England’s batting lineup and the emergence of young bowlers who have shown promise in high‑pressure situations. He also pointed out the strategic use of field placements and the coaching staff’s ability to adjust tactics mid‑series. Conversely, he identified key negatives: inconsistent wicket‑keeping performances, a lack of continuity in the spin department, and occasional lapses in concentration that cost the team valuable wickets. These issues, he argued, have prevented England from consistently capitalising on their early‑season momentum.

Looking ahead, Shemilt suggested that the next period—comprising the end‑of‑summer series and the forthcoming winter break—will be crucial for consolidating lessons learned. He expects the selectors to focus on strengthening the spin attack and refining the batting order, while the coaching team will likely implement targeted fitness and mental‑resilience programmes. The outcome of these adjustments will determine whether England can sustain an improved performance into the next season.
